what_it_does: Serving large language models at scale separates compute from memory: prefill (processing a prompt all at once) is compute-heavy and gets one cluster of GPUs, while decoding (generating one word at a time) is memory-bandwidth-heavy and gets another cluster. The problem: static scheduling leaves prefill GPUs overloaded while decoding GPUs sit idle, causing queuing delays. WindServe runs a global scheduler that constantly monitors both pools and dynamically shuffles jobs to balance load. It includes a smart rescheduling strategy that moves jobs between prefill and decoding without copying large key-value caches, and streams jobs to avoid interference between different kinds of work running on the same GPU.
